task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers answering who is responsible for repairing shared alleys in Bellfen. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Bellfen works register lists 238 alley segments, of which 142 have been formally accepted into the city's maintenance network.
The remaining 96 segments include private shared accesses and segments whose maintenance status still requires document review.
The register is a maintenance record, not by itself a final determination of land ownership or every user's access rights.
Regular public use or a city waste truck traveling through an alley does not automatically add that alley to the maintained network under the city's policy.
The issue resurfaced after residents on three connected blocks requested resurfacing of an alley used for waste collection and deliveries.
The city found that parts of the requested route appear in the maintenance register while an intervening segment does not.
Works manager Orin Vell said, "The route feels continuous when you walk it, but the records can assign different responsibilities along it."
Staff first compare the request's location with the register, earlier agreements and plans held by the city's property office.
When status is unresolved, the works department refers the document question to the property office rather than infer responsibility from the condition of the pavement.
The ordinary resurfacing budget is allocated to maintained segments; work on other land requires a separate approved arrangement.
An urgent temporary measure to keep an access open does not, under the supplied city procedure, automatically transfer permanent maintenance responsibility.
Residents may submit copies of agreements or older plans, but staff must assess those documents before changing the register.
Resident organizer Ena Marr said, "We need one answer about the paperwork before we can have a useful argument about the potholes."
A request can therefore produce a records inquiry, temporary work or a scheduled repair, depending on the segment and the problem identified.
The city does not guarantee that reporting a defect will result in city-funded resurfacing of the whole shared route.
Private owners can propose a maintenance agreement, but no standard fee or automatic acceptance offer is supplied in this packet.
The city plans a public map showing maintained segments with a notice that unresolved boundaries should be checked with staff.
The public map will not display private residents' contact details or substitute for obtaining advice about an individual property dispute.
Several older alley plans identify buildings by former business names that no longer appear on current street signs.
The works and property offices have begun a joint review of the three-block request but have not issued a final responsibility decision.
The waste collection schedule for those blocks remains unchanged while the records review continues.
The procedure described concerns Bellfen's records and policies and does not establish maintenance law for alleys elsewhere.

forbidden_additions: All alleys declared city property or all unlisted segments declared privately owned.
A final answer to the unresolved three-block request.
Automatic city responsibility based on public use, waste collection or a temporary repair.
preserve: Maintenance records distinguished from ownership and access questions.
Different responsibilities within an apparently continuous route.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
